notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached, no MuJoCo simulation was run, and no hardware or upstream-engine run is claimed. The card's entry_symbols list is empty, so there was no entry symbol to verify; the card's model sandbox/robots/humanoid.xml:16 exists in the clone.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card says family: ros and helper RosDriver, but the clone declares no ROS node, publisher, subscriber, service or action endpoint. cmake/ros.cmake and cmake/ros2.cmake are build helpers only. The upstream is a C++ physics engine whose Python binding re-exports the compiled simple_pywrap extension (bindings/python/simple/__init__.py:7) and exposes the C++ Simulator through SimulatorPythonVisitor (bindings/python/core/expose-simulator.cpp:12-14). The card's model is a MuJoCo MJCF, and the upstream runs that same file in MuJoCo with --mujoco (sandbox/humanoid_mj.py:115-116; sandbox/sim_utils.py:253-279), so the package uses the SDK MujocoDriver family (device kind world.sim, simulated, R0) for the model. The Simple-engine loop (sandbox/humanoid_mj.py:84-88) is not exposed: its class is C++/pybind, it is not installed here, and the clone has no Python step/reset class for a direct driver's native surface; inventing one would violate the upstream-surface rule.

SCOPE AND CONTRACT: the package serves the card's models[0] sandbox/robots/humanoid.xml. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [21 numbers]}} and checks each ctrl element against the model's actuator ctrlrange before writing data.ctrl; cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The model's 21 motors have no class attribute and inherit the top-level <motor ctrlrange="-1 1" ctrllimited="true"/> (sandbox/robots/humanoid.xml:36), so the published envelope is -1 to 1 per actuator. The state is the bridge's world state: 28 qpos (one free joint plus 21 hinges), 27 qvel and 21 ctrl; the model's option sets a 5 ms timestep (sandbox/robots/humanoid.xml:17). The model file is read from the read-only clone in place; no model or asset is copied.

FAKE AND DEPLOYMENT: backends['fake'] names the package class object FakeMujoco (the SDK's direct callable form), and driver.lock.json records the equivalent .fake:FakeMujoco entry point. The fake is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo and not upstream code. It parses the MJCF for the joint and actuator shape, the inherited ctrlrange and the timestep, but integrates a placeholder first-order motor model, does not integrate the free base, resolves no contact, tendon, joint-limit or force dynamics, and does not reproduce the model's qpos0 or four keyframes. MuJoCo was not importable where the gate ran (no network, no pip); the upstream itself says the dependency is optional and prints "Can't run, need to install mujoco" when absent (sandbox/sim_utils.py:11-17,253-255). A live backend therefore requires MuJoCo in the deployment environment, and no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine. The fidelity gaps list every difference.

WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the gate treats the callable fake backend as an upstream simulator, so it neither wraps it in a Recorder nor checks a native class surface; the fake is not upstream and no native calls are recorded. G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which the authoring guide's expected-warning list calls expected for simulator families. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised and no G4 warning remains.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds seven cases (model shape, control-vector length, inherited control envelope, step advancing the integration state, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass, and G9 passed. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. No site-limits.example.json is needed because the package declares no Limit and no operator-required bound; the control envelope is derived from the model at run time.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation (the clone has no ROS endpoint; the card's model sandbox/robots/humanoid.xml is stepped with mj_step by sandbox/sim_utils.py:253-279 in the --mujoco mode of humanoid_mj.py:115-116), all 23 facts against README.md, the bindings, the sandbox scripts and the MJCF, the ctrlrange-derived envelope (humanoid.xml:36, 204-225) and the stand-in fake. collect.py --strict failed on EXEMPLAR_RESIDUE because a gap named 'cartpole' (an exemplar term, and sandbox/robots has no such model file); the single fidelity declared the real engine (mujoco:Humanoid, F1) also for the fake stand-in, which runs no physics, and a test asserted that F1 contract on the fake; one fact added a 'so ...' inference to sim_utils.py:262. Reviewer changed driver.py (fidelity_by_backend gives the fake its own F0 'analytic:stand-in mujoco module (no physics)' contract with the stand-in gaps, the real-engine gaps reworded without the residue term, the timestep fact narrowed, and a fact that the served MJCF carries DeepMind's Apache-2.0 header, humanoid.xml:1-13), test_driver.py (the fidelity case expects the fake's F0 contract) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected MuJoCo-family warnings (G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, G8.NO_UNIT) and the digest unchanged. For the human reviewer: The package serves DeepMind's MuJoCo Humanoid model (Apache-2.0) as copied into the Simple sandbox, not the Simple engine; no hardware path exists. A live run needs the mujoco package; the sandbox's own MuJoCo mode steps at --dt (default 1e-3 s) with its own solver options, the package at the model's 0.005 s.
